land.text: the district of Murcia, which became independent as the Caliphate of Córdoba fell

predecessors.note: The Taifa page's infobox gives 'Downfall of Caliphate of Córdoba: 1011' but its text says 1031; the periods list starts the taifa in 1011. Cliopatria starts the row in 1015.

land.text: the remaining Murcian realm, 'absorbed by Castile, becoming the Kingdom of Murcia'

successors.note: Castile held the fortresses from the Treaty of Alcaraz (1243); the page's infobox 'Annexed by Castile: 1266'. The Aragonese conquest of 1265-1266 was made on Castile's behalf; the page also has Murcia 'transferred to the Crown of Aragon' in 1296 and incorporated in Castile in 1304 (Treaty of Torrellas), after the taifa.

capitals.name: Murcia
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Murcia. Under Almería, Valencia, Seville and the Almoravids (1014-1065 and 1078-1145) and under the Almohads (1172-1228) it was a provincial town; the dot is drawn only in the independent periods 1011-1014, 1065-1078, 1145-1172 and 1228-1266.

rulers.name: Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Iyad
rulers.note: Rulers list of the Taifa page. Ibn Faraj al-Thaghri is listed as a rival in 1146. No ruler is listed for 1011-1014 or 1065-1078.

rulers.name: Ibn Mardanish
rulers.note: The list says 1148-1172; the Ibn Mardanish page says 'king of Murcia from AD 1147 (AH 542) until his death' (d. 1172).

rulers.name: Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Yusuf Ibn Hud al-Mutawakkil
rulers.note: Assassinated at the gates of Almería in January 1238 (Ibn Hud page).

rulers.name: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Wathiq
rulers.note: First reign; he returns for a second reign from 1264.

rulers.name: Abu Ja'far Baha' al-Dawla Muhammad Ibn Hud
rulers.note: Swore fealty to Castile at Alcaraz in 1243 (Alcaraz page names the emir as Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Hud Baha al-Dawla).

rulers.name: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Wathiq
rulers.note: Second reign; the page gives no end year, only that he was overthrown between 1264 and 1266 by Abdallah ibn Ali of the Banu Ashqilula, allies of the Nasrids; 1266 is the page's annexation year.

correction.text: the Murcia core, unchanged, independent 1011-1014 (infobox 'Downfall of Caliphate of Córdoba: 1011')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page's periods list begins the taifa in 1011 ('from 1011 to 1014'); Cliopatria's row starts in 1015. Shape unchanged. The page gives no area; Cliopatria's 6,298 km2 is the Murcia district only.

correction.text: the same outline, held by Almería 1014-1038 and by Valencia 1038-1065, not by a Murcian state; the taifa is drawn only in 1011-1014, 1065-1078, 1145-1172 and 1228-1266

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws an independent Murcia for 1015-1033, but the page's infobox has Murcia 'To Almeria/Valencia: 1014-1038 / 1038-1065' and the text says it was 'ruled by the taifa rulers of Almería, Valencia, or Dénia' from 1012 to about 1049. The land is Almería's (then Valencia's), not a state of its own; the shape's outline is fine, its owner is not. Cliopatria's neighbours list shows Almería and Dénia touching it in 1015-1033.

correction.text: unchanged outline; years 1065-1078 only; 1078-1091 under Seville, 1091-1145 under the Almoravids (infobox 'To Seville/Almoravids: 1078-1091 / 1091-1145')

keyframe_review.note: The shape (Murcia core, 6,298 km2) is right for the independent years, which the page gives as 'from 1065 to 1078' (Cliopatria starts a year late, in 1066). From 1078 to 1091 Murcia was 'under the forcible control of Seville, by Abbad II al-Mu'tadid', so 1079-1084 should not be Murcia's. Shape unchanged, years 1065-1078 only.

New keyframe: the page lists independence 'in 1145' (Abd Allah ibn Iyad, 1145-1147; Ibn Faraj al-Thaghri a rival in 1146) while the infobox has Murcia 'To Valencia: 1145-1147'. The outline is the Murcia core as Cliopatria draws it from 1147; the pages disagree, so this is a low-certainty bridge.

correction.text: the Murcia core plus Valencia province, which passed to Ibn Mardanish in August 1147, and Castellón province (the castle of Montornés, 1147/8)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1147 shape (9,404 km2) is the Murcia core only. Taifa of Valencia page: Ibn 'Iyad's forces passed to Ibn Mardanish in August 1147, rulers list 'Ibn Mardanish: 1147-1172' (the earlier 'ok' verdict, which left Valencia out until 1152, is corrected on the reviewer's finding, eu-12-g 2026-10-25). Years 1147-1148 only; Dénia follows in 1149. No infobox area.

correction.text: 'He established his rule over the cities of Murcia, Valencia and Dénia': the Murcia core, Valencia and Castellón provinces and Alicante province

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Dénia (Alicante province) is Ibn Mardanish's by June 1149 at the latest (Genoese funduqs 'at Valencia and Dénia'); about 32,100 km2 against Cliopatria's 9,404 for 1147-1151. The page gives no date for the gain itself (confidence 1 in the ledger).

Kept as Cliopatria draws it (77,869 km2, bbox 3.4 W to 0.6 E, 36.9 N to 41.5 N); unverified: no page opened bounds the realm. The earlier cut to 27,800 km2 (Murcia, Valencia, Alicante) is withdrawn (reviewer eu-12-g, 2026-10-25): it dropped Castellón, which the Ibn Mardanish page has under him in 1147/8, and the lands the Spanish article names. Area check: no page gives an area; the four named provinces (Murcia core, Valencia, Castellón, Alicante) are about 32,100 km2, so Cliopatria is 2.4 times that, but the outline also holds the lands in the east that the Spanish article gives him (Segura, Baza, Guadix, Úbeda, Albarracín), so the shape is not shown wrong. Disagreements with the Spanish article: Jaén district 1159 (the outline has it from 1152), Écija and Carmona (1158-1160, lost 1161: outside the outline, not drawn), Tortosa, Lérida and Fraga lost 1148-1149, Almería 1165-1169 (Almería page). Years end in 1167 because Albarracín is ceded by 1168.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1152 outline without Albarracín, ceded to Pedro Ruiz de Azagra between 1165 and 1168

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the one year between the Albarracín cession (by 1168, Spanish article) and Cliopatria's 1169 withdrawal of the north-east strip to the Crown of Aragon.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1169 outline without Albarracín, for 1169-1172 only; 1172-1228 Almohad

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria 70,031 km2, kept (unverified, as the 1152 shape), minus the Albarracín circle. The years are wrong at the end: Ibn Mardanish died in 1172 and 'In 1172 Murcia was taken by the Almohads' (infobox 'To the Almohads: 1172-1228'), so 1173-1176 belong to the Almohad Caliphate. Almería: the Almería page puts Ibn Mardanish's control of the city at 1165-1169 and the Spanish article has it defecting to the Almohads in 1171; not separated here.

correction.text: 'seize most of al-Andalus relatively unopposed, except Valencia': the Murcia core and Andalusia without Andújar, Baeza and Martos

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Murcian shape for 1177-1235. Ibn Hud's rebellion began in May 1228 with the defeat of the governors of Murcia and Valencia; he took 'most of al-Andalus relatively unopposed, except Valencia, where he was opposed by Zayyan ibn Mardanish'. 'Most of al-Andalus' is the page's phrase; Valencia is excluded (the earlier outline included the Valencia region: corrected on the reviewer's finding, eu-12-g 2026-10-25) and so are Castile's 1225 gains Andújar, Baeza and Martos. No page lists his cities, so the Andalusia reading is soft and probably generous at the edges.

correction.text: as 1228-1231 without the region of Jaén, where Ibn Nasr 'elevated himself to sultan in 1232'

keyframe_review.note: Ibn Nasr takes Jaén in 1232 (Ibn Hud page; Muhammad I page: 'In the same year, Muhammad took Jaén'); Arjona is his from 16 July 1232.

correction.text: as 1232-1233 without Niebla and its district ('Niebla: 1234-1262')

keyframe_review.note: Niebla is a taifa again from 1234 (Taifa overview list). Ibn Nasr's month in Seville in 1234 is not a change of holder (it 'returned to Ibn Hud's rule').

correction.text: as 1234-1235 without Córdoba, 'taken over by Ferdinand III of Castile in 1236'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's shape for 1236-1240 (7,849 km2) is the Murcia core only; that is right only from 1239. In 1236 Córdoba falls but Granada (1237), Almería and Seville with the west (1238) and Málaga (1239) are still Ibn Hud's or his successors' on the pages (this replaces the 'ok' verdict and the unsourced 1236 bridge to 'nobody', reviewer eu-12-g 2026-10-25). Years 1236 only.

correction.text: as 1236 without Granada ('In 1237, Granada accepted Ibn Nasr as its ruler')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Granada goes to Ibn Nasr in May 1237 (Muhammad I page).

correction.text: the Murcia core and Málaga province: Ibn Hud assassinated in January 1238 at the gates of Almería; Almería to Ibn Nasr, Seville and the west to the Banu al-Bajji (placeholder)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Almería passes to the Emirate of Granada in 1238 (Almería page); Seville and the south-west are held by an unnamed local power (confidence 1 in the ledger); Málaga follows in 1239.

correction.text: the Murcia core, Cliopatria's 7,849 km2 outline, after Ibn Nasr took Málaga in 1239

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's 1236-1240 outline is right for 1239-1240 only. Taifa overview list: 'Lorca: 1240-1265 (to Castile)' and 'Orihuela: 1239/1240-1249/1250 (to Murcia or Castile)' suggest Lorca was already a taifa of its own in 1240; the Treaty of Alcaraz page has Lorca, Mula and Cartagena refusing the 1243 treaty and Lorca and Mula conquered in 1244. The outline is kept.

Muhammad ibn Hud Baha al-Dawla, 1241-1262. The 7,849 km2 outline is right for 1241-1243 and is kept as Cliopatria draws it to 1249; the cut is carried by the ledger (Lorca and Mula conquered in 1244: 'Lorca and Mula were conquered in 1244'; 'Cartagena fell to Alfonso in the spring of 1245') and by the 1250 keyframe, not by this shape (verdict was 'adjust' to the post-1245 outline for all of 1241-1249, which removed those districts twice; reviewer eu-12-g, 2026-10-25). No infobox area.

correction.text: the 1241 shape without Lorca and Mula (conquered 1244) and Cartagena (taken in spring 1245)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row ends in 1249 but the page keeps the taifa to 1266 ('from 1228 to 1266 when it was absorbed by Castile'). Same outline as the post-1245 correction: a Castilian vassal with Castilian garrisons (Alcaraz page) until the Mudéjar revolt of 1264-1266 and the Aragonese conquest of 1265-1266.

region.text: the city of Murcia and its district, Cliopatria's core shape (6,298 km2)

ledger.note: 1011: Murcia becomes an independent taifa as the Caliphate of Córdoba falls. The page lists the taifa 'from 1011 to 1014' and its infobox gives 'Downfall of Caliphate of Córdoba: 1011' (the text says 1031 and lists Murcia as ruled by Almería, Valencia or Dénia from 1012 to about 1049); the page names no founder.

region.text: the city of Murcia and its district, Cliopatria's core shape (6,298 km2)

ledger.note: 1014: Murcia passes to Almería. Infobox 'To Almeria/Valencia: 1014-1038 / 1038-1065' (Almería to 1038, then Valencia, still without a Murcian state); the text has it 'ruled by the taifa rulers of Almería, Valencia, or Dénia' from 1012 to about 1049. Cliopatria nevertheless draws a Murcian state 1015-1033.

region.text: the city of Murcia and its district, Cliopatria's core shape (6,298 km2)

ledger.note: 1065: Murcia is independent again. The page lists independence 'from 1065 to 1078' after the infobox's Valencian period (1038-1065); Cliopatria's second shape starts in 1066.

region.text: the city of Murcia and its district, Cliopatria's core shape (6,298 km2)

ledger.note: 1078: Seville takes Murcia. 'From 1078 until 1091 it was under the forcible control of Seville, by Abbad II al-Mu'tadid.' Cliopatria keeps a Murcian shape to 1084. The Taifa page's infobox continues 'To Seville/Almoravids: 1078-1091 / 1091-1145', but the 1091/92 hand-over to the Almoravids is Seville's loss, not Murcia's, so this dossier no longer carries a separate 1091 event (deleted on the reviewer's finding, eu-12-g 2026-10-25; the Almoravid dossier's ledger/18 records 'In late 1091 or January 1092, Ibn Aisha, one of Ibn Tashfin's sons, seized control of Murcia' and its counterpart should be taifa-of-seville).

region.text: the Murcia core

ledger.note: 1145: Murcia is independent again under Abd Allah ibn Iyad. The page lists independence 'in 1145' and the ruler 1145-1147; the infobox, however, has 'To Valencia: 1145-1147'. In 1146 Ibn Iyad 'recognized the supremacy of the Hudid ruler Sayf al-Dawla' after throwing off Almoravid authority (the Hudid vassalage is not mirrored here: Sayf al-Dawla has no dossier in this batch).

1147: Ibn Mardanish takes Murcia. 'king of Murcia from AD 1147 (AH 542) until his death' (the Taifa page's rulers list says 1148-1172); the same state, with the dynasty of the Wolf King in place of Ibn Iyad's.

region.text: Valencia province and, with it, Castellón province (the castle of Montornés)

ledger.note: 1147 (August): Valencia passes to Ibn Mardanish. Taifa of Valencia page: 'Ibn 'Iyad was killed in August 1147, but before he died he managed to pass the command of Valencia's forces to' 'Muhammad ibn Sa'd ibn Mardanish, known simply as Ibn Mardanish'; its rulers list gives 'Ibn Mardanish: 1147-1172' and 'He based himself in Murcia and placed Valencia under the governorship of his brother Yusuf.' Reviewer eu-12-g (2026-10-25) corrected the date from Cliopatria's 1152 (confidence 1). Castellón province is added from the Ibn Mardanish page (second page): 'In the first year of his rule (1147/8), Ibn Mardanish faced the rebellion of his relative, Yusuf ibn Hilal,' based 'in the castle of Montornés', and sent 'his prisoner to Xàtiva'; the page does not name the province (the castle stands above Benicàssim in Castellon province: the reviewer's and the researcher's identification, not the page's). The region is therefore a reading: 2.

region.text: Alicante province, where Dénia lies

ledger.note: 1149 (June, latest): Dénia is in Ibn Mardanish's hands. The page says only that 'He established his rule over the cities of Murcia, Valencia and Dénia' (no date; as Almoravid power declined), and that his truce of June 1149 with Genoa 'permitted the establishment of Genoese funduqs at Valencia and Dénia': a terminus ante quem, not a territorial statement, so confidence 1. Reviewer eu-12-g (2026-10-25): the earlier entry used Cliopatria's 1152 and named taifa-of-denia, but the Dénia dossier has no state between 1076 (ledger/11, its loss to Zaragoza) and 1224; the Almoravids are named as the power in decline, the page does not say who held Dénia in 1147-1149. The Almohad dossier's ledger/17 (Dénia gained from taifa-of-denia in 1152, confidence 1) conflicts with this and with the 1172 Almohad takeover below: flagged to af-02.

region.text: the rest of Cliopatria's 1152 outline (about 49,600 km2: parts of Albacete, Cuenca, Teruel, Tarragona, Jaén, Granada and Almería provinces) beyond the Murcia core and the Valencia, Castellón and Alicante provinces

ledger.note: 1152: Cliopatria's outline jumps from 9,404 to 77,869 km2. Dated by pages above: Valencia (1147) and Dénia (by June 1149); nothing opened dates the rest. The Spanish article shows that his dominions did reach beyond those three: he 'extendió sus dominios a Jaén (1159), Baza y Guadix', his father-in-law Ibn Hamushk 'le cedió el distrito de la sierra de Segura', and Albarracín was his until 1165-1168 (below); it also has 'Tortosa (1148), Lérida (1149) y Fraga (1149)' taken from him by Ramón Berenguer IV. The page dates the Jaén district to 1159, not 1152, so the outline is early in the east and possibly wide in the north. Bridge only, kept at Cliopatria's year so that the outline is not dropped on page silence (reviewer eu-12-g, 2026-10-25); confidence 1 is a gap for a gap-filler.

region.text: Lorca and the Guadalentín valley

ledger.note: 1165: the Almohads march on Lorca. In September-October 1165 Ibn Mardanish 'led a large army from Murcia to defend Lorca against an Almohad force advancing from the castle of Vélez'; at al-Fundūn in the Guadalentín valley 'they were routed' at Faḥṣ al-Jullāb.

region.text: the former territory of the Banu Razin (Albarracín), about 25 km around the town

ledger.note: 1168 (latest): Albarracín leaves Ibn Mardanish. Spanish article: 'Más adelante entre 1165 y 1168, en pago a la ayuda militar proporcionada contra los almohades' he 'cedió el antiguo territorio de los Banū Razīn (Albarracín) al Señor de Estella, Pedro Ruiz de Azagra'. The page gives a range, so 1168 is its upper bound; the 25 km circle is a reading of the territory. Cliopatria's 1152 and 1169 outlines both contain Albarracín (5 of the circle's 7 cells), i.e. the cession is not drawn there. Gazetteer name needed: Albarracín (place, Teruel).

region.text: the north-eastern strip of Cliopatria's 1152 outline (lat 40.5 to 41.4, lon -0.8 to 0.6; about 8,350 km2)

ledger.note: 1169: the north-east of the outline is withdrawn. Cliopatria's shape falls from 77,869 to 70,031 km2 in 1169, and the strip lies wholly inside Cliopatria's Crown of Aragon of 1169. No page opened dates a loss here; the Spanish article has 'tomara Tortosa (1148), Lérida (1149) y Fraga (1149)' (Ramón Berenguer IV), earlier than the 1152 outline, so the outline may be too wide in the north. Bridge only (confidence 1).

region.text: Lorca and the Guadalentín valley

ledger.note: 1172: the fighting over the Murcian frontier ends with the Almohad takeover (see the loss event).

region.text: Ibn Mardanish's realm at his death: Cliopatria's 1169 outline without Albarracín (Murcia, Valencia, Dénia and the lands between)

ledger.note: 1172: the Almohads take Murcia. 'In 1172 Murcia was taken by the Almohads' (infobox 'To the Almohads: 1172-1228'). Second page, Taifa of Valencia: 'Valencia annexed by the Almohads in 1172' and 'Only after he died in 1172 did the Almohads take his kingdom, with little opposition' (Spanish article: he died at Murcia on 28 March 1172 and his son Hilal 'se apresuró a declararse vasallo de los almohades'). Confidence 2 (was 3): the Murcia page names only Murcia and the Valencia page only Valencia, so the rest of the outline is a reading (reviewer eu-12-g, 2026-10-25).

region.text: most of al-Andalus: the eight Andalusian provinces except Andújar, Baeza and Martos (Castilian from 1225); Valencia is excluded

ledger.note: 1228: most of al-Andalus, except Valencia, passes to Ibn Hud. The Almohad caliph 'was forced to depart Seville with his remaining soldiers', 'allowing Ibn Hud to seize most of al-Andalus relatively unopposed, except Valencia, where he was opposed by Zayyan ibn Mardanish' (Almohad page: 'with Spain practically all lost, al-Ma'mun abandoned Seville', October 1228). 'Most of al-Andalus' is the page's phrase and the page lists no towns, so the region is the researcher's reading: Andalusia (Almería, Cádiz, Córdoba, Granada, Huelva, Jaén, Málaga, Sevilla) minus Andújar, Baeza and Martos, which Castile held from 1225 (kingdom-of-castile ledger/43). Valencia is excluded (reviewer eu-12-g, 2026-10-25). Badajoz and Extremadura (Ibn Hud lost a battle to León near Mérida) are not drawn: no page names a town there. The Almohad dossier's ledger/46 gives the Murcian state the whole rest of Almohad Spain and Portugal in October 1228; the two readings differ in the west and are left for af-02.

1228: the Banu Hud rule Murcia. Ibn Hud 'pledged allegiance to the Abbasid caliphs in Baghdad' and took the titles Amir al-Mu'minin and al-Mutawwakil (no year on the page); same state, new dynasty after the Almohad interval.

region.text: the governorate of Murcia (Cliopatria's 1236 core, 7,849 km2)

ledger.note: 1228 (May): Ibn Hud takes Murcia. 'Ibn Hud began a rebellion in May 1228, quickly winning popular support and defeating the governors of Murcia and Valencia.' The same page then says he seized most of al-Andalus 'except Valencia, where he was opposed by Zayyan ibn Mardanish', and the Taifa of Valencia page has Zayyan 'remained independent of Ibn Hud' (rulers list 'Zayyan ibn Mardanish: 1228/9-1238'; the Almohad dossier's ledger/44 gives Valencia to taifa-of-valencia in 1228). So the region is Murcia only; the Valencia region of the earlier entry is dropped (reviewer eu-12-g, 2026-10-25). The page does not say where he first rose; the Taifa page lists him as ruler of Murcia 1228-1238.

region.text: the plain around Jerez

ledger.note: 1231: Castile defeats Ibn Hud. 'his troops were decisively defeated by the Kingdom of Castile in the Battle of Jerez, and also by León near Mérida.'

region.text: the region of Jaén

ledger.note: 1232: Ibn Nasr rises at Jaén. He 'elevated himself to sultan in the region of Jaén' while Ibn Hud held most of al-Andalus (Jaén as Ibn Hud's land is the researcher's reading); Ibn Hud 'was at first able to defeat Ibn Nasr in 1234'. Second page, Muhammad I of Granada: 'On 16 July 1232, a mosque assembly in Arjona declared the town's independence. In the same year, Muhammad took Jaén.' After 1234 he 'kept his rule over a small region containing Arjona, Jaén, Porcuna, Guadix, and Baeza' as Ibn Hud's nominal subject.

region.text: Niebla and its district (Cliopatria's 1236 Niebla outline plus the capital)

ledger.note: 1234: Niebla leaves Ibn Hud's realm. The Taifa overview's list of the third taifas has 'Niebla: 1234-1262 (to Castile)'. The year is the page's; that the previous holder was Ibn Hud rather than the Almohads is the researcher's reading (Ibn Hud page: 'seize most of al-Andalus relatively unopposed' from 1228; Almohad dossier ledger/46: the Almohads are out of Iberia in October 1228). The Niebla dossier's ledger/4 gives the same land from the Almohads (confidence 2, lowered by the reviewer); its counterpart should be taifa-of-murcia. Niebla dossiers were not touched in this repair (verdict fix).

region.text: the plain around Jerez

ledger.note: 1235: the Jerez contest with the Kingdom of Castile is closed in the last year of that state's dossier (kingdom-of-castile ledger/45 dissolves it into crown-of-castile in 1235). The Ibn Hud page gives nothing between Jerez (1231) and the fall of Córdoba (1236), so the end year is the researcher's reading; Córdoba itself is carried by the 1236 loss to crown-of-castile. Replaces a 1236 end that named kingdom-of-castile after its dossier had ended (reviewer eu-12-g, 2026-10-25).

region.text: Córdoba

ledger.note: 1236: Córdoba falls to Castile. Ibn Hud 'was not able to protect Córdoba from being taken over by Ferdinand III of Castile in 1236' (Almohad page: 'Córdoba fell to Christian forces in 1236').

region.text: Granada

ledger.note: 1237: Granada goes to Ibn Nasr. 'In 1237, Granada accepted Ibn Nasr as its ruler.' Second page, Muhammad I of Granada: 'In May 1237 (Ramadan 634 AH), by invitation of the city's notables, he took Granada, which he then made his capital.'

region.text: Almería and its province

ledger.note: 1238: Almería passes to Ibn Nasr. 'After Ibn Hud's assassination in Almería in 1238' the bulk of the remaining Muslim-controlled territories passed to the ruler 'constituting the Emirate of Granada, to which Almería belonged from then on' (Almería page); Ibn Hud page: 'assassinated in January 1238 at the gates of Almería'. Second page, Muhammad I of Granada: 'He also took Almería in 1238 and Málaga in 1239.' The year is the pages'; the province for the city is a reading. Mirrors the Almohad dossier's ledger/45 (Almería to taifa-of-murcia in 1228). Added on the reviewer's finding (eu-12-g, 2026-10-25).

region.text: Seville and the rest of Ibn Hud's Andalusia: the remainder of Sevilla, Cádiz, Huelva and Córdoba provinces

ledger.note: 1238 (after Ibn Hud's assassination in January): Seville and the south-west leave the Murcian realm. No page opened says who held them: the Ibn Hud page is silent after his death; the Taifa of Seville page ends in 1091; the History of Seville page jumps from 1228 to the Castilian conquest ('The city surrendered on 23 November 1248'); the Siege of Seville page has only 'Seville and Granada were the only major cities in the Iberian Peninsula that had not acquiesced to Christian suzerainty' (1246); the Taifa overview's third-taifa list has no Seville entry. The only Seville family any page names is the Banu al-Bajji, who in 1234 helped Ibn Nasr take Seville, 'but he was only able to hold it for one month' before it returned 'to Ibn Hud's rule' (Muhammad I page). They are named here as a placeholder holder at confidence 1, not on a page's say-so. Replaces the earlier 1236 bridge to 'nobody' (which double-counted Granada and Almería); Córdoba (1236), Jaén (1232), Niebla (1234), Granada (1237), Almería (1238) and Málaga (1239) are dated separately. Gap: who held Seville and the west from 1238 to 1248.

region.text: Málaga and its province

ledger.note: 1239: Málaga passes to Ibn Nasr. 'He also took Almería in 1238 and Málaga in 1239.' The page adds that he 'did not take these southern cities by force, but through political maneuvering and the consent of the inhabitants'. That Málaga was part of the Murcian realm until then is a reading (Ibn Hud held 'most of al-Andalus'); confidence 2. Added on the reviewer's finding (eu-12-g, 2026-10-25).

1243: Murcia swears fealty to Castile (April, Treaty of Alcaraz). The emir 'proposed vassalage to Castile', the Murcian rulers accepted 'vassalage to the Castilian monarch', 'Castilian troops would occupy the fortresses of the region' and Castile took a share of the taxes. The state, its dynasty and its colour continue to 1266; the vassal tint belongs to Castile's dossier (vassal_start, counterpart taifa-of-murcia), which no event type in this one can carry.

region.text: Lorca and Mula

ledger.note: 1244: Castile conquers Lorca and Mula. 'Lorca and Mula were conquered in 1244.'

region.text: Cartagena

ledger.note: 1245: Cartagena falls to Alfonso. 'Cartagena fell to Alfonso in the spring of 1245', with naval help from the Cantabrian coast.

region.text: the 1241 shape without Lorca and Mula (conquered 1244) and Cartagena (taken in spring 1245)

ledger.note: 1266: Murcia is absorbed by Castile. The taifa existed 'from 1228 to 1266 when it was absorbed by Castile, becoming the Kingdom of Murcia' (infobox 'Annexed by Castile: 1266'); the Mudéjar revolt of 1264-1266 had 'effectively nullified' Alfonso X's obligations under Alcaraz, and the page links the 'Conquest of Murcia (1265-1266)'.

wars.name: Battle of Fahs al-Jullab
wars.outcome: Almohad victory: Ibn Mardanish's army was routed in the Guadalentín valley in September-October 1165 and Murcia fell to the Almohads in 1172.
wars.note: The Ibn Mardanish page dates the battle to Dhū l-Qaʿdah 560 (September-October 1165); the Taifa page gives 1165 and 1172.

wars.name: Ibn Hud's rebellion against the Almohads
wars.outcome: Ibn Hud overthrew the Almohad governors from May 1228 and took most of al-Andalus except Valencia (Zayyan ibn Mardanish); Castile (Jerez 1231, Córdoba 1236) and Ibn Nasr (Jaén 1232, Granada May 1237, Almería 1238, Málaga 1239) took it back; Ibn Hud was assassinated at the gates of Almería in January 1238.

wars.name: Castilian campaigns against Ibn Hud
wars.outcome: Castile defeated Ibn Hud at Jerez in 1231 and took Córdoba in 1236.
wars.note: The Ibn Hud page names the battle of Jerez and the fall of Córdoba, not the campaigns between; the war name is the researcher's. The contest event at Jerez closes in 1235 because the Kingdom of Castile dossier ends then; the Córdoba loss (1236) is to the Crown of Castile.

wars.name: Conquest of Murcia in 1243
wars.outcome: Murcia accepted Castilian vassalage at Alcaraz in April 1243 and garrisons in its fortresses; Lorca and Mula fell in 1244 and Cartagena in spring 1245.
wars.note: Alcaraz page: by early 1243 the emir 'faced threats from the Order of Santiago and the Nasrid Kingdom of Granada'.

wars.name: Mudéjar revolt of 1264-1266
wars.outcome: The revolt 'effectively nullified' Alfonso X's obligations under the Treaty of Alcaraz; Murcia was absorbed by Castile in 1266 after the Aragonese conquest of 1265-1266.
wars.note: The Aragonese part is only a link title ('Conquest of Murcia (1265-1266)') on the Taifa page, which was not opened.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the pages name towns and provinces (Murcia, Valencia, Dénia, Lorca, Mula, Cartagena, Jaén, Granada, Almería), not boundaries. The Murcia core is Cliopatria's. The 1152-1172 outline is Cliopatria's, unverified (Valencia from 1147 and Dénia by 1149 are page-dated; the rest is a confidence-1 bridge). The 1228-1239 outlines are readings of 'most of al-Andalus except Valencia', shrinking by dated losses (Jaén 1232, Niebla 1234, Córdoba 1236, Granada 1237, Almería and the south-west 1238, Málaga 1239).

sources.title: Taifa of Murcia
sources.note: Identity, periods of independence (1011-1014, 1065-1078, 1145, 1147-1172, 1228-1266), the infobox timeline, rulers, 1172, 1243, 1266.

sources.title: Muhammad ibn Sa'd ibn Mardanish
sources.note: The Wolf King: 'king of Murcia from AD 1147', Murcia, Valencia and Dénia, Fahs al-Jullab (1165). Thin: no dates for his conquests, no death account.

sources.title: Treaty of Alcaraz
sources.note: April 1243 vassalage, garrisons, Lorca and Mula (1244), Cartagena (1245), the revolt of 1264-1266.

sources.title: Ibn Hud
sources.note: The rebellion of May 1228, Jerez 1231, Ibn Nasr 1232 and 1237, Córdoba 1236, assassination January 1238. The article title is 'Ibn Hud' (Muhammad ibn Yusuf ibn Hud under longer titles would not load).

sources.title: Almohad Caliphate
sources.note: Context only: Almohad control of Iberia by about 1170-1172, al-Ma'mun leaving Seville in October 1228, Córdoba 1236, Murcia 1243.

sources.title: Taifa of Valencia
sources.note: Repair: Ibn 'Iyad's death in August 1147 and Valencia's forces passing to Ibn Mardanish; rulers list 'Ibn Mardanish: 1147-1172'; Valencia annexed by the Almohads in 1172; Zayyan ibn Mardanish independent of Ibn Hud 1228/9-1238.

sources.title: Muhammad ibn Mardanis (Spanish Wikipedia)
sources.note: Repair: the extent of his realm (Jaén 1159, Baza, Guadix, Úbeda, Segura, Écija and Carmona 1158-1160, Albarracín ceded 1165-1168, Tortosa 1148, Lérida and Fraga 1149 lost), death on 28 March 1172.

sources.title: Muhammad I of Granada
sources.note: Repair: Jaén 1232, Seville for one month in 1234, Granada in May 1237, Almería 1238, Málaga 1239.

sources.title: Almería
sources.note: Repair: Ibn Mardanish's control 1165-1169, Ibn Hud 1228, his assassination in Almería in 1238 and the city passing to the Emirate of Granada.

sources.title: Taifa
sources.note: Repair: list of the third taifas (Niebla 1234-1262, Lorca 1240-1265, Orihuela 1239/1240-1249/1250, Murcia 1228-1266); no Seville entry after 1091.

sources.title: History of Seville
sources.note: Repair: silent on 1228-1246; the Castilian conquest, the city surrendering on 23 November 1248.

sources.title: Siege of Seville
sources.note: Repair: 1246, Seville and Granada the only major cities not under Christian suzerainty; silent on who ruled Seville after 1228.

notes: Repaired 2026-10-25 on the reviewer's findings (eu-12-g). Cliopatria rows: 1015-1033 and 1066-1084 draw an independent Murcia where the page has a dependency (1014-1065) and a Sevillan occupation (1078-1091); 1169-1176 runs to 1176 though the Almohads took Murcia in 1172; 1177-1235 and 1250-1266 have no shape. The 1152-1176 outlines (77,869 and 70,031 km2) are kept as Cliopatria draws them, unverified: no page opened bounds the realm, and the cut to Murcia, Valencia and Dénia (27,800 km2) made in the first pass is withdrawn because it dropped Castellón and the eastern lands the Spanish article gives Ibn Mardanish. Valencia is dated to 1147 (Taifa of Valencia page), Dénia to June 1149 at the latest (Genoese treaty; confidence 1), the rest of the outline is a confidence-1 bridge at 1152; Albarracín leaves by 1168 and a north-eastern strip goes to the Crown of Aragon in 1169 (bridge). Ibn Hud's realm: 'most of al-Andalus, except Valencia' (1228) is read as Andalusia without Castile's 1225 gains, shrinking by dated losses (Jaén 1232, Niebla 1234, Córdoba 1236, Granada May 1237, Almería 1238, Málaga 1239); who held Seville and the south-west from 1238 to 1248 is page-silent and the Banu al-Bajji are a placeholder (confidence 1). The Taifa of Murcia page contradicts itself (downfall of the Caliphate 1011 or 1031; Almohads to 1228 versus an independent kingdom 1223-1243 and annexation 1243, 1266 or 1304). Not recorded for want of a dated frontier: Écija and Carmona (1158-1160, Carmona lost 1161), Almería under Ibn Mardanish (1165-1169 or 1171), the 1171 rebellions of Lorca, Elche, Alcira and Baza, Quesada lost in 1171. Mirrors the other dossiers should carry: Almoravid ledger/18 (1092 Murcia) should name taifa-of-seville; Almohad ledger/17 (Dénia 1152 from taifa-of-denia) should be 1172 from taifa-of-murcia; Almohad ledger/46 (rest of Almohad Spain and Portugal to Murcia) is wider than the Andalusia drawn here; Niebla ledger/4 (1234) should name taifa-of-murcia; Valencia: Ibn Mardanish 1147-1172 and Zayyan 1228/9-1238; Emirate of Granada: Jaén 1232, Granada May 1237, Almería 1238, Málaga 1239; Castile: Córdoba 1236, Lorca and Mula 1244, Cartagena 1245, vassal_start 1243 and vassal_end 1266 (counterpart taifa-of-murcia); Crown of Aragon: the 1169 strip. Pages not opened for want of budget: Battle of Fahs al-Jullab, Conquest of Murcia in 1243, Conquest of Murcia (1265-1266), Taifa of Almería. Gazetteer names needed: Mula, Jerez de la Frontera, Albarracín (places); Al-Andalus (region, better than Andalusia). The Hudid vassalage of 1146 (Sayf al-Dawla) and the Order of Santiago have no dossiers here. Vassalage seen from the vassal's side has no ledger event type; it is carried as a rename caption in 1243.
